dataset.name: Seedling census and natural enemy survey data at a tropical understory forest warming experiment (TRACE) in Puerto Rico from 2015-2017
description: The data in this package were used to evaluate the effects of a natural drought and in situ experimental warming on density-dependent feedbacks on seedling demography at the Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE) in Luquillo, Puerto Rico from June 2015 through June 2017. The TRACE site consists of three control plots and three plots that are experimentally warmed using infrared heaters. Seedling surveys at each plot were conducted each year and data including seedling height, root collar diameter, leaf counts, mortality, etc. were measured. Aboveground natural enemy surveys were conducted annually during the seedling surveys. Leaves from each seedling were assessed for damage, and the number of unique damage morphotypes were counted for the following natural enemies: gall makers, grazers, endophytes, leaf miners, and pathogens. Additionally, Guarea guidonia seedlings from outside of each plot were collected in 2017 and root morphology data were collected using root scans. Note: Complete metadata is available within the download file. This metadata can be viewed with esri ArcGIS software or by viewing the imbedded .xml file. Coverages and grids contain a file called metadata.xml and shapefiles contain a file called (shapefile_name.xml). These files can be exported to FGDC and ISO metadata formats.

measurementTechnique:
The Tropical Responses to Altered Climate Experiment (TRACE) is an understory forest warming experiment in Luquillo, Puerto Rico that consists of six hexagonal plots that are 4 meters (m) in diameter. Three of the plots are control plots, and three are experimentally warmed +4˚Celsius relative to the control plots using infrared heaters. For a full site and experiment description, see Kimball et al. (2018).
SEEDLING SURVEYS
The seedling surveys were conducted as follows: seedlings >10 centimeters (cm) but less than 2 m in height were initially tagged and identified to species in June 2015, and surveys were conducted in the fall of 2015 following a drought from April-August 2015, June 2016, and June 2017. The experimental warming began in the fall of 2016, so the June 2017 survey reflects the initial response to warming. Measurements included seedling root collar diameters, heights, leaf counts, seedling status, percent of damage (see NATURAL ENEMY SURVEYS methods section), and treatment (drought, experimental warming, or control). Conspecific density was calculated each year as the number of conspecific (same species as focal seedling) seedling neighbors within each plot. Heterospecific density was calculated in each year as the number of heterospecific (different species than focal seedling) seedling neighbors within each plot.
NATURAL ENEMY SURVEYS
The aboveground natural enemy surveys were conducted at the time of the seedling surveys. Briefly, foliar damage was assessed visually for each seedling by estimating the percent of leaf damage ranging from 0-100%. Foliar damage is included in the “TRACE_seedlingSurvey.csv” file. In half of each experimental plot, up to five leaves per seedling were photographed each year and later used to identify leaf damage morphotypes. Damage morphotypes were then classified into five guilds of natural enemies: gall makers, grazers, endophytes, leaf miners, and pathogens. The number of unique damage morphotypes within each of these categories was recorded. For additional details on the seedling and natural enemy surveys, see Bachelot et al. (2020).
ROOT MORPHOLOGY
In June 2017, Guarea guidonia seedlings were collected outside of the TRACE plots and scanned using WinRHIZO software (Regent Instruments, Inc.) to obtain root morphology data. Eight seedlings were collected at 2 and 4 m outside of each plot, for a total of 48 seedlings. Seedlings were placed in transparent and sterile bags for transportation to the laboratory before scanning. Root morphology data that were collected included root length, volume, number of tips/forks/crossings, and root lengths for specific diameter classes.
